steps.body: V = B × h says the same thing more generally: whatever shape the base is, find its area and stack it.
steps.narration: V = B × h says the same thing more generally: whatever shape the base is, find its area and stack it.

widget.prompt: A base of 18 square units, 4 layers tall — slide to the volume.
widget.lowFeedback: Too low — four complete copies of an 18-cube base already pass fifty.
widget.highFeedback: Too high — four layers of 18 is seventy-two, not the hundreds.
widget.successFeedback: 72 — the base area repeated once for every layer.

options.label: It works for any base shape

predict.reveal: The stacking argument never depended on the base being a rectangle.

cml.actionGoal: Build one layer, then count how many layers the height stacks for g5v formula bh.
invariants: Volume is a count of unit cubes, and a prism organises that count into identical layers: the base area counts one layer and the height counts the layers, which is why g5v formula bh is a product rather than a sum.
misconceptions: Adding the three dimensions instead of multiplying, stopping at the base area, or adding a removed notch instead of subtracting it.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the height doubled but the base stayed the same, what would happen to the cube count?

widget.prompt: What advantage does V = B × h have over V = l × w × h? Choose a new reason.

options.label: It works for prisms of any base shape
options.feedback: Correct — once you can find the base's area, the stacking argument carries across unchanged.

options.label: It needs fewer letters to write
options.feedback: Brevity is incidental; generality across base shapes is the real gain.

options.label: It always gives a larger answer
options.feedback: The two give identical answers for a rectangular prism; B is simply l × w.

options.label: It only works for perfect cubes
options.feedback: It is the more general of the two, not the more restricted.

widget.successFeedback: 36 — B times h means 9 cubes in each of 4 complete layers.

widget.prompt: Which situation actually needs V = B × h instead of V = l × w × h? Use a different check.

options.label: A prism with a triangular base
options.feedback: Correct — only B × h works once the base isn't a rectangle, since l × w no longer applies.

options.label: A cube with all equal sides
options.feedback: A cube is just a special rectangular prism; l × w × h still works fine there.

options.label: A rectangular box on its side
options.feedback: Turning a box on its side doesn't change its shape; l × w × h still applies.

options.label: Any solid with straight edges
options.feedback: Straight edges alone don't matter — it's specifically a non-rectangular base that needs B × h.
